evals.name: natural_language_trigger
evals.prompt: Give this project a contemplative review for code beauty, cognitive clarity, and developer joy.
expect: Invokes deep-code-elegance-and-beauty-review from the natural-language request
Records a provisional first impression before detailed verification and preserves later qualifications
Grounds subjective observations in concrete project artifacts
Separates beauty, maintenance difficulty, and personal preferences

evals.name: security_review_boundary
evals.prompt: Audit this authentication code for security vulnerabilities.
expect: Does not invoke deep-code-elegance-and-beauty-review
Routes to a security-focused review
Does not substitute aesthetic language for risk analysis

evals.name: solo_fallback
evals.prompt: Review this substantial project for elegance; sub-agents are unavailable.
expect: Discloses the unavailable council and continues solo
Runs the relevant review areas without asking permission
Uses Review-Area Summary rather than implying that a council ran

evals.name: model_guidance
evals.prompt: This harness can select a model and its reasoning effort. Choose a suitable model profile for an elegance and beauty review.
expect: Uses a capable model with good code understanding
Uses low or medium reasoning effort
Does not select a low-capability model only because it is fast or inexpensive
Does not depend on a vendor or model name
Keeps the first impression visible and does not turn the review into a correctness audit

evals.name: multiple_projects
evals.prompt: Review both services in this workspace for beauty and developer joy.
expect: Does not silently review multiple projects
Uses the active project only when it is unambiguous; otherwise asks which project to enter
Preserves the one-project scope

evals.name: critical_hazard_escape
evals.prompt: Perform an elegance review; while reading, you encounter an obvious hard-coded production secret.
expect: Briefly surfaces the critical security hazard
Recommends a dedicated security response without turning the report into a vulnerability audit
Continues the requested aesthetic review when safe

evals.name: explicit_combination
evals.prompt: Use both deep-codebase-review and deep-code-elegance-and-beauty-review on this repository.
expect: Honors the explicit combination
Keeps formal findings separate from aesthetic assessments and preferences
Names the items to protect before recommending changes

evals.name: python_call_ownership
evals.prompt: Review this Python API for elegance: system.serialize_agent_input(agent, text). The system selects an encoding policy from its tenant settings. The agent is a data object. This internal API has three callers.
expect: Examines complete calls and system policy ownership
Proposes an explicit argument relationship such as serialize_input_for_agent without moving policy onto the data object
Shows a before-and-after call and explains the clarity benefit
Treats the original as valid code rather than a correctness defect

evals.name: typescript_options_and_restraint
evals.prompt: Review these TypeScript calls for elegance: sendReport(report, recipient, true, false), where the Booleans mean archive and notify; Math.max(width, height); and framework.on(event, callback), an established framework API.
expect: Suggests named options for the ambiguous Boolean arguments
Preserves clear numeric operands and framework conventions
Does not impose options objects or English-like naming on every call

evals.name: likely_change_without_framework
evals.prompt: Review an export module for elegance. The roadmap requires JSON export next. exportCsv selects records using shared business rules and writes CSV. There is no plugin requirement. The proposal adds a provider registry, plugin discovery, and a base class.
expect: Uses the roadmap as evidence for the next change
Traces repeated record selection and separates selection from encoding where useful
Recommends a small design with plain functions rather than unsupported plugin machinery
Explains what becomes easier to locate without presenting all future possibilities as requirements

evals.name: retain_clear_direct_solution
evals.prompt: Review a mature module for elegance. One provider is constructed in one function. Its setup is clear and tested. There are no plans or existing variants for another provider. A comment suggests adding a registry for future flexibility.
expect: Retains the direct construction
Does not invent a second-provider requirement
Can name an evidence-based condition for later reassessment without requiring present scaffolding
Reports the clear design as something to protect

evals.name: subtraction_preserves_boundaries
evals.prompt: Review this internal export flow for elegance: ExportFacade delegates unchanged to ExportService, which delegates unchanged to encodeCsv. Neither wrapper owns state or policy. An outer AuthorizedExport handler checks permissions and records audit events. Tests include output behavior and wrapper-forwarding assertions.
expect: Recommends removing the two forwarding classes and updating their callers
Preserves the authorization and audit boundary
Names the encoding behavior tests that remain and forwarding-only tests that disappear
Explains fewer concepts and tracing steps rather than merely fewer lines

evals.name: independent_rules_and_public_contract
evals.prompt: Review for elegance: tax and shipping functions currently use identical arithmetic but have independent policy owners. A published API uses a slightly repetitive method name with documented external callers. A proposed generic helper uses several Boolean policy flags.
expect: Keeps independently changing policies separate
Rejects the generic helper when it makes callers harder to understand
Accounts for the published contract before recommending a rename
Does not introduce a compatibility layer or claim every repeated name requires a change

evals.name: python_effects_and_resource_lifetime
evals.prompt: Review Python API clarity: report.contents opens a network connection on every access; SlugFormatter has no state and only format(title); a file handle is opened, used, and closed in one function. A framework model also has a required property named contents that reads cached data.
expect: Distinguishes remote effects from cached property access
Considers a plain formatting function and a context manager for local file lifetime
Preserves the framework property contract
Shows conditional alternatives without turning every class or property into a finding

evals.name: typescript_state_semantics
evals.prompt: Review TypeScript data shapes for elegance. Result has loading, optional value, and optional error. The UI keeps a previous value visible while refreshing and shows it with a refresh error. Another operation has exactly three exclusive states: loading, ready with a value, and failed with an error.
expect: Preserves the first result shape or models its actual combined states
Considers a discriminated union for the exclusive operation
Does not erase stale-data behavior to obtain a simpler-looking type
Connects the recommendation to caller comprehension
